data.narrative:
Silicon Quantum Computing, founded by Michelle Simmons, is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised A$83M to date. The quantum computing sector comprises a fragmented peer universe of 11 total comparable companies—3 publicly traded (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

The peer-median method is inapplicable to this valuation. The quantum computing sector contains only 5 same-sector peers overall, but filtering for companies at the same development stage (Series A), adjacent stages, or similar valuation tiers yields fewer than three datapoints in any single cohort. Constructing a meaningful median from such a sparse filtered set would introduce substantial bias. The public comparables (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) span different maturity profiles and business models, limiting their direct relevance to an early-stage private fundraise.

The absence of sufficient narrow peer data points reflects the nascent and heterogeneous nature of the quantum computing market, where stage, technical approach, and path to revenue vary widely across competitors. Without a robust triangulation method, no single valuation range can be derived from this analysis. Any forward valuation of Silicon Quantum Computing would require supplementary data—including financial projections, proprietary technical differentiation, or third-party transaction comps—to establish defensible value anchors. The current dataset supports only a comparative landscape assessment, not a point or range estimate.
